source2: Colonial Williamsburg Foundation, 'Oyo Empire', Slavery and Remembrance - https://slaveryandremembrance.org/articles/article/?id=A0121
notes: Ilorin, an Oyo province seized by Fulani and in the Sokoto Caliphate from c.1823, destroyed Oyo-Ile c.1835; capital moved south to New Oyo. Coded T2 treating Fulani Ilorin as external; T1a if Ilorin counted internal. Afonja's 1817 revolt.

notes: Islam Khan's campaigns (1608-11) took Sonargaon (April 1611); before end of 1611 all Bara-Bhuiyans including Musa Khan submitted and were held at Dhaka (Jahangirnagar). External Mughal conquest. Database end 1612 slightly late.

Satsuma and Choshu led conspirators' Kyoto coup (3 Jan 1868) ousted Yoshinobu and proclaimed imperial rule; brief civil war; feudal domains replaced by prefectures by 1871. Failed 1866 Choshu expedition. Shogunal seat was Edo, not Kyoto.

Valois house ruled France 1328-1589 without break; 1450 is a periodization boundary (Normandy reconquered 1449-50). Prior crisis: Armagnac-Burgundian conflict, English control of Paris until royal troops re-entered c.1436.

successor: Ethiopia Kingdom III (Zemene Mesafint; Ras Mikael Sehul, later Yejju regents)
source1: Library of Congress Federal Research Division, Ethiopia: A Country Study, 'Contact with European Christendom' - http://countrystudies.us/ethiopia/12.htm
notes: 1769: Ras Mikael Sehul of Tigray had kings murdered and ruled through a puppet; Gondar emperors became figureheads while autonomous nobles warred until 1855 (LoC). Internal fragmentation, no external conquest. Database start 1621 vs Fasilides 1632.

Britannica: in 552 Turkish tribes living within the empire rebelled and, allied with Wei, destroyed the Juan-juan; Turks then ruled Mongolia. Internal under vassal rule (T2 if Turks deemed external). Rouran remnants destroyed 555.

French under Faidherbe occupied Fouta in the late 1850s (Britannica); Umar Tal's recruitment weakened the almamy. Leads date treaty annexations 1859 and final occupation of central Futa 1890-91; end date uncertain. Sources thin.

notes: Babylonian kingship passed from Nabu-shumu-libur to Simbar-Shipak, a Sealand soldier, founding the Second Sealand Dynasty in Babylon; mechanism undocumented, apparatus apparently continued. Aramean pressure was external. Low confidence.

Grenet: Kidarites expelled from Balkh 467 by Sasanian-Hephthalite operations (after Hephthalite rebellion from 457); residual Gandhara kingdom sent embassies to China until 477. Gandhara's later takeover by Alchon Huns is not detailed in opened sources; inferred.
